elements.quote: Nevertheless, Cochrane Reviews have been greatly under-utilised in guidelines and recommendations are often based on lowerlevel evidence or expert consensus because of limitations regarding familiarity, awareness, usefulness, access, and time [12-21].
elements.reason: The introduction describes gaps in current knowledge/use in guidelines (under-utilisation and reasons), but it does not explicitly articulate “important uncertainties” in the sense of unresolved questions needing clarification.

elements.quote: Yet, if a review does not provide evidence to strengthen or change recommendations or is not used by guideline developers, the review could potentially have very limited impact on healthcare and may be considered a poor use of time, funds, and resources.
elements.reason: The rationale explains why conducting the review matters: guideline uptake affects healthcare impact and resource use.

elements.quote: Limited research has explored the use of NMAs to inform guidelines [38]. Lunny et al summarised how often NMAs and PW-MAs support recommendations in a sample of 50 guidelines [15]. Our article is the first to systematically search for reviews and summarise their citation in guidelines, and to explore the citation of reviews in depth.
elements.reason: When prior similar work exists (e.g., Lunny et al.), the need for this review is explained and previous research is cited; the manuscript also claims novelty relative to prior work.
No proposed mechanism of action is described for the intervention effects (no brief mechanism is provided in the retrieved introduction/background evidence).
The retrieved evidence does not include a logic model showing hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes.

elements.quote: We aimed to summarise which, when, where, who, and why Cochrane Reviews that applied NMA were cited in guidelines; and to compare the citation of NMA reviews in guidelines with PW-MA reviews.

elements.quote: We aimed to summarise which, when, where, who, and why Cochrane Reviews that applied NMA were cited in guidelines; and to compare the citation of NMA reviews in guidelines with PW-MA reviews.
elements.reason: This is a review of how Cochrane reviews are cited in clinical guidelines (citation/uptake), not a review of intervention effects where planned intervention comparisons would be stated using PICO or a variant.

elements.quote: Our findings are consistent with previous work. Korfitsen et al found that only 18% of 585 recommendations made in 56 guidelines published by the Danish Health Authority between 20142021, included evidence from a Cochrane Review [13]. Lunny et al found that 249 reviews (of which 64% were systematic reviews using PW-MAs and 3% using NMAs) were cited in 50 guidelines (dated 2017-2018) retrieved from the TRIP and Epistemonikos databases [15].
elements.reason: The Discussion interprets the results by comparing them with prior studies and stating consistency with previous work.

elements.quote:
Wefound that some guidelines cited low quality evidence and out-dated reviews. Of the 26 NMAreviews that were cited in guidelines, 50% reported heterogeneous results, 19% reported inconsistent results, 73% reported low and very low credibility results, and 15% included studies with a high risk of bias.

Furthermore, reviews require regular updating to include newly published studies or apply new methods that would alter findings [3]. As general guidance, the Cochrane recommends updating reviews at least every two years [3]. Yet, we found that 42% of cited NMA reviews were first cited between 2-6 years after publication, therefore guidelines may be citing out-dated reviews.
elements.reason: The discussion describes limitations related to the evidence used in included reviews (e.g., low/very low credibility, heterogeneity/inconsistency, high risk of bias) and issues with evidence currency (outdated reviews and delayed updating). However, it is not explicitly framed as “limitations of the evidence included in the review” in a comprehensive, structured way.

The provided discussion content describes reasons for low guideline impact (e.g., heterogeneity, inconsistency, credibility, risk of bias, need for updating) but does not explicitly discuss limitations of the review processes used in this systematic review.
Because limitations of the review processes used are not explicitly discussed, the potential impact of each such limitation on the results is also not explicitly discussed in the retrieved evidence.
